.qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/task:read-only text scan of authored files, including test prompts and golden source
evidence: Workbook Quality Checks!D53 explicitly bars an unpinned remote fetch anywhere in the task. The frozen task/environment/Dockerfile:1 uses the mutable tag node:22-bookworm-slim and lines 5-7 run apt-get update/install without package versions or an apt snapshot. Frozen task/tests/Dockerfile:1-2 likewise uses mutable node:22-bookworm-slim and python:3.12-slim tags; lines 12-14 run unversioned apt-get update/install, and line 35 invokes Playwright install --with-deps, which can also resolve current system packages. These are verbatim frozen-template Dockerfiles (SHA256 environment 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1; tests 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd), so this is a workbook-versus-template conflict, not a task-specific added download. Other row-52 checks were clean in the authored content: task.toml:34 contains only ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}; the seed has snippets: []; the solution package manifest uses exact versions; all 178 remotely resolved package-lock entries have versions and integrity values; a read-only text scan found no live-key shapes, host-machine user path, or instruction-override phrase in authored files. No build or full judge run was performed for this row.
counterexample: The same frozen submission built at two later dates can pull different node/python tag contents or Debian packages while keeping identical task bytes. A conforming alternative using digest-pinned bases and a fixed Debian package snapshot would not have this drift.
suggested_fix: Resolve the workbook/template conflict in the shared template: pin image digests and the Debian package source/versions, then regenerate and re-freeze the candidate; do not patch this task copy alone.
